Round 1 of review. Measured head `754ab29f7aab253c26981159034d292cc45d4256`, still the PR head when this verdict was written (`ev/HEAD.txt`). Role contract: merge base is origin/main, so the `dev/governance/roles/` diff is empty.

## Block

Mandatory check (1) of the brief needs a control in which the same payload without `merge_queue` is accepted. The record has none. All five recorded POSTs (`mq-probe/01`, `03a` to `03d`) are refusals. The `03*` bodies are negative controls: they show that a malformed rule and an unknown type fail schema validation, while the well-formed rule is refused by name. That separates "schema error" from "named rule refused". It does not show that the rest of the request is acceptable from this caller on this repository: the name, the `refs/heads/probe/mq-r10` condition, the enforcement, and ruleset-write permission for that token. Only an accepted body proves those. The grant covers exactly that case ("one ruleset scoped to a probe branch ... and the ruleset's deletion"). It needs one accepted POST, for example `01` with `required_status_checks` only (or a no-op rule) on `refs/heads/probe/mq-r10`, recorded with its 201 and id. Then one DELETE of that id, a GET of it reading back 404, and a rulesets list reading back the same three ids (#1300).

The likely conclusion still stands. The 422 names `merge_queue`, and the owner is `User` (`ev/owner-and-probe-branch.txt`). The adopt recommendation for all five groups probably survives the re-probe unchanged. This is a block because the brief made the control mandatory and the record does not have it.

## Findings

- No positive control (the block above). Add one accepted POST of the payload minus `merge_queue`, then one DELETE and the read-backs. Restate the control table and the Null control section of the body with that row. Carry: R10-FLOW-MQ-PROBE
- The record overstates the GraphQL read. `mq-probe.md` says "The GraphQL read agrees". But `repository.mergeQueue(branch:"main")` is `null` on any repository that has no queue configured on `main`, organization-owned or not. So `05-graphql-mergequeue.json` cannot tell "User-owned, so no queue is possible" apart from "no queue configured". It corroborates only the owner type. Reword the sentence so it stops presenting the read as independent agreement. Carry: R10-FLOW-MQ-PROBE
- The `## Head` section describes history that does not exist. It says `754ab29` "merges the authored code head `f1eb42a` and then merges origin/main `dfcd8d9be` ... into this PR's previous head". The real chain is `754ab29` (parent `f1eb42a`) on top of `f1eb42a` (parent `dfcd8d9be`), with no merge commit (`ev/head-ancestry.txt`). The second sentence of the section is correct. Correct the first so a later carry check does not look for a resolution delta that is not there. Carry: R10-FLOW-MQ-PROBE
- "The five held groups" does not match the roster on main. R10-FLOW-RECORD-PITCH, R10-FLY-ROW-HEAD-CARRY and R10-FLY-CARRY-DOC-CONTEXT each have an `after` edge on R10-FLOW-MQ-PROBE. R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE has `after: []`: the orchestrator ruling of 2026-10-24 under mandate 6329234399 put its edge back to none, and its stage is `queued`. R10-FLOW-BODY-ONLY's `after` is `[R10-UPDATE-PR-SIGNALS, R10-FLOW-BODY-PATCH]`, so part (a) is held by carry text only. The five names and their order match carry [2] exactly, and every recommendation is adopt, so the outcome does not change. The orchestrator's release edit should still remove three edges, not five, and record TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE as already released. Carry: R10-FLOW-MQ-PROBE
- The job `if:` census leaves `tests / fast (3.14)` unchecked (`mq-probe/08`), and the record says so. The queue is infeasible, so the `merge_group` wiring stays dormant; the census has to be re-run only if the repository ever moves to an organization. Carry: dismissed: the wiring is dormant while the queue is infeasible; the record already names re-running the probe on any owner move.

## Evidence

- RESULT check (1), refusal shape: re-derived from the recorded files. `01` and `03a` return `{"errors":["Invalid rule 'merge_queue': "]}`. `03b`, `03c` and `03d` return `Invalid property /rules/0: data matches no possible input`. The 422 names the `merge_queue` rule, not an unrelated field. The positive control is missing (Block). The documentation fetch for merge-queue availability did not return the availability sentence for me either, so the owner-type attribution is still inference, as the record says.
- RESULT check (2), rulesets: a read-only GET today returns `22628467 main-protect`, `23698884 main-protect-checks` and `23937752 release-tags-protect`. Their `updated_at` values match `mq-probe/12` (the same instants, stated in UTC instead of +02:00). No probe ruleset is left behind, and `GET branches/probe/mq-r10` is 404 (`ev/rulesets-get.tsv`, `ev/owner-and-probe-branch.txt`). No DELETE was owed because nothing was created.
- RESULT check (3), groups: carry [2] of R10-FLOW-MQ-PROBE in `dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json` on main names R10-FLOW-RECORD-PITCH, R10-FLY-ROW-HEAD-CARRY, R10-FLY-CARRY-DOC-CONTEXT, R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE and part (a) of R10-FLOW-BODY-ONLY. The record's table and the body name exactly these five. The after-edge mismatch is in Findings.
- RESULT check (4), host paths: no host or home path is in the added lines of the diff, and none is in this verdict's `ev/`.
- RESULT check (5), classification: `tests/entities.py` (PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub) prints `2 of 2445 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED` at the head and also at merge base `dfcd8d9be`. The sets of failing check names are identical (`gate-sweep.yml: ...` and `graders-head-copy's delivery_status step ...`; this environment fails both on both sides). "force the FULL" appears zero times. `closure.py select --diff <merge-base>` at the head prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run, 33 scoped out.` (`ev/entities-*.txt`).
- Merge: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 754ab29` exits 0 with tree `0822a718a` (`ev/merge-tree.txt`). origin/main equals the merge base.
- CI on the head: 37 success, 17 skipped, 1 failure (`ev/ci-check-runs.tsv`). The failure is `governance / delivery-status`, which reports OVERDUE for #2762 and #2795, not for this PR. The PR's own row is present. Its log says it is not a required context and does not block (`ev/delivery-status-red.txt`). The body's "None known at handoff" predates CI and owes nothing for this check.
- Not applicable: mutation proof, step 1. The diff has no production line or check. `VERSION`, the manifest and the notes heading are untouched. No claim file moved.
- Figures not re-derived: the CI-minute sums in `mq-probe/11` (I did not re-sum job durations), the prelude self-test count of 29, and the `gate.REQUIRED` 18/19 split. They are context only and do not bear on the block.
